modules.title: Soil Formation (Pedogenesis)
modules.html:
Meaning of Soil

Soil is the loose, unconsolidated top layer of the earth's crust composed of weathered rock materials (minerals), organic matter, water, air and living organisms, which supports plant growth. The study of soil formation is called pedogenesis.

Factors of Soil Formation

Soil formation is influenced by five major factors, often summarised as: $$Soil = f(Parent\ material, Climate, Organisms, Relief, Time)$$

  • Parent material: the rock or deposited material from which soil is formed; determines initial mineral composition and texture.
  • Climate: temperature and rainfall control the rate of weathering; hot, wet climates like Nigeria's rainforest zone favour rapid chemical weathering.
  • Organisms (living things): plants, animals and microorganisms contribute organic matter, aid nutrient cycling and mix soil layers (bioturbation).
  • Relief (topography): slope and elevation affect drainage, erosion and soil depth; steep slopes tend to have thinner soils due to erosion.
  • Time: the duration over which weathering and soil development processes have acted; older soils are generally more developed and weathered.

Weathering: The First Stage of Soil Formation

  1. Physical (mechanical) weathering: breakdown of rocks into smaller particles without chemical change, caused by temperature fluctuation, frost action, and abrasion by wind or water.
  2. Chemical weathering: decomposition of rock minerals through reactions such as hydrolysis, oxidation, carbonation and hydration, common in Nigeria's humid tropical climate.
  3. Biological weathering: breakdown of rocks by the action of living organisms, e.g. plant roots penetrating cracks and burrowing animals.

Processes Following Weathering

After weathering produces regolith (loose rock fragments), further processes such as humification (formation of humus from decomposed organic matter), leaching (downward movement of soluble materials) and translocation of clay contribute to full soil development into distinct horizons.

Weathering TypeAgent/ProcessExample
PhysicalTemperature changeExfoliation of granite
ChemicalHydrolysis, oxidationRusting of iron minerals
BiologicalRoot actionRoot wedging in rock cracks

The rate of weathering in tropical Nigeria is generally higher than in temperate regions because high temperature and rainfall accelerate both chemical and biological weathering processes.

examples.q: Explain why soils in Nigeria's rainforest zone are generally more deeply weathered than soils in temperate regions.
examples.a: Nigeria's rainforest zone has high rainfall and high temperature throughout most of the year. These climatic conditions accelerate chemical weathering reactions (hydrolysis, oxidation) and support abundant biological activity (roots, microorganisms), both of which occur much more slowly in cooler, drier temperate climates. Consequently, over time this leads to deeper and more intensely weathered soils in the rainforest zone.

examples.q: Differentiate between physical and chemical weathering, giving one example of each.
examples.a: Physical weathering is the mechanical breakdown of rock into smaller fragments without any change in chemical composition, e.g. exfoliation of granite due to alternating heating and cooling. Chemical weathering involves a change in the chemical composition of rock minerals through reactions such as oxidation, e.g. the rusting (oxidation) of iron-bearing minerals in rock to form iron oxide.

modules.title: Soil Profile and Soil Horizons
modules.html:
Meaning of Soil Profile

A soil profile is a vertical section or cross-section of soil from the surface down to the unweathered parent rock, showing a sequence of distinct layers called horizons. Studying the soil profile helps agriculturists understand soil fertility, drainage and suitability for various crops.

The Major Soil Horizons

  • O horizon (organic layer): the topmost layer composed of fresh and decomposing organic matter such as leaf litter.
  • A horizon (topsoil): dark-coloured layer rich in humus and organic matter, most fertile and biologically active; where most plant roots and soil organisms are concentrated.
  • E horizon (eluviation layer): a zone (not always distinct in tropical soils) where clay, minerals and organic matter are leached downward.
  • B horizon (subsoil): a zone of accumulation (illuviation) where materials leached from above (clay, iron and aluminium oxides) are deposited; generally less fertile, more compact, with less organic matter.
  • C horizon (regolith/parent material): partially weathered parent rock material from which the soil above developed.
  • R horizon (bedrock): the unweathered solid rock underlying the soil profile.

Characteristics Distinguishing the Horizons

HorizonColourOrganic MatterTexture/Structure
A (Topsoil)Dark brown/blackHighLoose, granular
B (Subsoil)Reddish/yellowish brownLowCompact, blocky
C (Parent material)Variable, rock-likeVery low/nonePartially weathered rock

Depth Measurements in Soil Profile Study

Soil scientists dig a soil pit (profile pit) and measure the thickness of each horizon from the surface downward. If the depth to the top of horizon B is \(d_A\) and the depth to the top of horizon C is \(d_B\), then the thickness of horizon B, \(T_B\), is given by: $$T_B = d_B - d_A$$

Total soil depth is important agriculturally because it determines the volume of soil available for root penetration and the amount of water and nutrients the soil can hold for crop use.

examples.q: In a soil profile pit, horizon A extends from 0 cm to 25 cm, and horizon B extends from 25 cm to 70 cm. Calculate the thickness of horizon B.
examples.a: Using \(T_B = d_B - d_A\), where \(d_A = 25\,cm\) (depth to top of B) and \(d_B = 70\,cm\) (depth to top of C): \(T_B = 70 - 25 = 45\,cm\). Horizon B (the subsoil) is 45 cm thick.

examples.q: Explain why the A horizon (topsoil) is generally more fertile than the B horizon (subsoil).
examples.a: The A horizon is more fertile because it contains a higher concentration of organic matter (humus) derived from decomposed plant and animal residues, supports greater biological activity from soil organisms that release nutrients, and has a loose, granular structure that favours root penetration, aeration and water infiltration, unlike the compact, organic-matter-poor B horizon where materials are mainly deposited by leaching from above.

modules.title: Physical Properties of Soil Related to Formation and Profile
modules.html:
Soil Texture

Soil texture refers to the relative proportion of sand, silt and clay particles in a soil, and is determined largely by the parent material and degree of weathering. Texture affects water-holding capacity, aeration, drainage and nutrient retention. Soils are classified using the textural triangle into classes such as sandy, loamy and clayey soils.

Soil Structure

Soil structure describes the arrangement of soil particles into aggregates called peds. Common structural types include granular (common in fertile topsoil), blocky (common in subsoil), platy and columnar structures. Good granular structure improves aeration, root penetration and water infiltration.

Soil Bulk Density and Porosity

Bulk density is a key physical property that varies across soil horizons and reflects compaction and organic matter content. It is defined as: $$\rho_b = \frac{M_s}{V_t}$$ where \(M_s\) is the mass of oven-dried soil solids and \(V_t\) is the total volume of the soil sample (including pore spaces). Topsoil (A horizon) typically has a lower bulk density than compacted subsoil (B horizon) due to higher organic matter content and looser structure.

Total porosity, \(f\), the fraction of soil volume occupied by pore spaces, is related to bulk density and particle density, \(\rho_p\) (commonly taken as 2.65 g/cm³ for mineral soils), by: $$f = \left(1 - \frac{\rho_b}{\rho_p}\right) \times 100\%$$

Significance of Physical Properties in Agriculture

  1. Soils with lower bulk density and higher porosity allow better root penetration, aeration and water infiltration, favouring crop growth.
  2. Heavily compacted subsoils (high bulk density) restrict root growth and drainage, often limiting crop yield.
  3. Understanding the texture and structure of each horizon helps farmers decide tillage methods and depth of ploughing.
PropertyTopsoil (A)Subsoil (B)
Bulk densityLower (~1.1-1.3 g/cm³)Higher (~1.4-1.6 g/cm³)
Organic matterHighLow
StructureGranularBlocky/compact

Field measurement of bulk density typically uses the core sampling method, where a known volume of undisturbed soil is extracted, oven-dried and weighed to compute \(\rho_b\).

examples.q: A core sample of topsoil has a volume of 100 cm³ and an oven-dry mass of 125 g. Calculate the bulk density of the soil.
examples.a: Using \(\rho_b = M_s/V_t\): \(\rho_b = 125\,g / 100\,cm^3 = 1.25\,g/cm^3\). This is a typical bulk density for a well-structured, organic-matter-rich topsoil.

examples.q: Using a bulk density of 1.325 g/cm³ and particle density of 2.65 g/cm³, calculate the total porosity of the soil sample.
examples.a: Using \(f = (1 - \rho_b/\rho_p)\times 100\%\): \(f = (1 - 1.325/2.65)\times 100\% = (1 - 0.5)\times 100\% = 50\%\). The soil has a total porosity of 50%, meaning half its volume is occupied by pore spaces (air and water).

quiz.q: The scientific study of soil formation is known as
quiz.solution: Pedogenesis is specifically the process/study of soil formation, while pedology is the broader study of soils in general.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five major factors of soil formation?
quiz.solution: The five soil-forming factors are parent material, climate, organisms, relief and time; market price of crops is an economic factor, not a soil-forming factor.

quiz.q: The type of weathering that breaks down rock through temperature fluctuations without changing its chemical composition is called
quiz.solution: Physical (mechanical) weathering breaks rocks into smaller fragments through processes like temperature change, without altering chemical composition.

quiz.q: The rusting (oxidation) of iron-bearing minerals in rocks is an example of
quiz.solution: Oxidation, which changes the chemical composition of the mineral (forming iron oxide), is a form of chemical weathering.

quiz.q: Nigeria's rainforest soils tend to be more deeply weathered than temperate soils mainly because of
options: higher temperature and rainfall accelerating weathering
quiz.solution: High temperature and rainfall in the rainforest zone accelerate both chemical and biological weathering processes, leading to deeper weathering.

quiz.q: A vertical section of soil from the surface to the parent rock, showing distinct layers, is called a
quiz.solution: A soil profile is the vertical cross-section of soil revealing the sequence of horizons from surface to bedrock.

quiz.q: Which soil horizon is generally the most fertile and richest in organic matter?
quiz.solution: The A horizon (topsoil) has the highest organic matter (humus) content and biological activity, making it the most fertile horizon.

quiz.q: The B horizon is also referred to as the zone of
quiz.solution: The B horizon (subsoil) is the zone of illuviation where materials leached from the A horizon above (clay, oxides) accumulate.

quiz.q: The unweathered solid rock underlying the soil profile is called the
quiz.solution: The R horizon represents the unweathered bedrock lying beneath all other soil horizons.

quiz.q: In a soil pit, horizon A extends from 0-20 cm and horizon B extends from 20-60 cm. The thickness of horizon B is

options: arrangement of soil particles into aggregates
relative proportion of sand, silt and clay particles
quiz.solution: Soil texture is defined by the relative proportions of sand, silt and clay particles present in a soil sample.

quiz.q: Soil bulk density is calculated using the formula
quiz.solution: Bulk density is defined as the mass of oven-dried soil solids divided by the total volume of the soil sample: \(\rho_b = M_s/V_t\).

quiz.q: A core sample has volume 80 cm³ and dry mass 104 g. Its bulk density is
If bulk density is 1.06 g/cm³ and particle density is 2.65 g/cm³, the total porosity is approximately
Compared to the B horizon, the A horizon typically has
options: higher bulk density and lower organic matter
lower bulk density and higher organic matter
the same bulk density and organic matter
quiz.solution: The A horizon (topsoil) generally has lower bulk density (looser, granular structure) and higher organic matter content than the more compact B horizon.
